study type: Secondary analysis of a national, observational, prospective, population-based cohort study
exposure: Non-IVF fertility treatment (including insemination and ovarian stimulation)
cohort: 8823 Women with a twin pregnancy who gave birth at or after 22 weeks of gestation in France
finding: Women with twin pregnancies after medically assisted reproduction (MAR) had a 30% higher risk of serious maternal complications compared to women with natural twin pregnancies.
mod_finding: The study found that planned mode of delivery was a potential intermediate factor influencing the association between mode of conception and severe acute maternal morbidity in twin pregnancies, but did not report specific findings related to mode of delivery.
